title: Resolvent convergence for sample second-moment matrices with heterogeneous profile
problem: Can quantitative deterministic equivalents for the resolvent of the uncentered sample second-moment matrix (1/n) X X^T be established when the columns are independent but not identically distributed, possibly non-centered, and with arbitrary dependence among the coordinates of each column?
setting: X in R^{p x n} with independent columns x_i, finite second moment Sigma_i = E[x_i x_i^T], no i.i.d. assumption, no centering, no entrywise independence within a column. Spectral parameter z fixed in the open upper half plane; the regime Im z -> 0 is not treated. Bounds are dimension-explicit and hold in L^q. Assumptions enter only through moments of centered quadratic forms.
method: A finite-profile self-consistent fixed-point system extending the Marchenko-Pastur scalar equation. A deterministic module proves existence, uniqueness, Stieltjes-transform structure, compact support and stability of the profile equation. A probabilistic module uses resolvent replacement, leave-one-out identities and L^q moments of centered quadratic forms x_i^T B x_i - tr(Sigma_i B), normalized by either the Hilbert-Schmidt or the operator norm of the test matrix.
contribution: Quantitative comparison bounds for tr(A(G^z - G-tilde^z)) under weak quadratic-form control only: no subgaussian assumption, no global concentration property, no independence among column coordinates, no limiting profile distribution, no common covariance. Profile-adapted estimates distinguish the Hilbert-Schmidt and operator test geometries; a k commuting-values profile incurs only linear-in-k loss; the centered i.i.d. case recovers Marchenko-Pastur with an explicit rate under any moment strictly above two.

mathematical_objects.name: Resolvent deterministic equivalent
mathematical_objects.role: The deterministic matrix G-tilde^z approximating the random resolvent; the whole paper is about validating it quantitatively under weak hypotheses.

mathematical_objects.name: Self-consistent equation
mathematical_objects.role: The finite family of coupled equations defining the deterministic equivalent; its stability estimate transfers random fluctuations into deterministic error.

mathematical_objects.name: Marchenko-Pastur law
mathematical_objects.role: The scalar limit the profile equation generalizes and the benchmark recovered in the centered i.i.d. special case.

mathematical_objects.name: Centered quadratic forms
mathematical_objects.role: The sole channel through which model assumptions enter; their L^q moments, normalized by Hilbert-Schmidt or operator norm, index all the bounds.

mathematical_objects.name: Leave-one-out / resolvent perturbation identities
mathematical_objects.role: Decompose the resolvent column by column so that each increment is governed by one quadratic form.

mathematical_objects.name: Stieltjes transform
mathematical_objects.role: Encodes the empirical spectral distribution and gives the deterministic equivalent the analytic structure (Nevanlinna / real-measure) used for existence and support control.

mathematical_objects.name: Second-moment profile
mathematical_objects.role: The unrestricted family (Sigma_i) that parametrizes the model; the point is that no structural condition (diagonalizability, isotropy, convergence) is placed on it.

limitations: Conclusion section not matched by the extractor; card built from abstract and introduction.
Estimates hold only at fixed z in the upper half plane; these are not local laws and say nothing about the spectral edge or the real axis.
The k commuting-values bound loses a factor linear in k.
No analysis of mean-induced outliers or of separating a deterministic mean from centered noise.
open_questions: The deterministic-equivalent validity is decoupled here from entrywise independence and from any limiting profile distribution, which are exactly the assumptions random-matrix-based statistics results usually impose. The bound holds strictly more generally than its current applications assume.
Whether the regime Im z -> 0 (a local law) is reachable under the same quadratic-form-only hypotheses, without sub-Gaussianity or global concentration.
cross_domain_note: Directly relevant to statistics: covariance and precision estimation, spectral clustering, random-features analysis, all of which invoke Marchenko-Pastur-type deterministic equivalents typically under i.i.d. entries or a fixed population covariance.

title: Spectral Independence and Local-to-Global Techniques for Optimal Mixing of Markov Chains
problem: What condition on a high-dimensional distribution over vertex labelings of a graph guarantees that simple Markov chains such as Glauber dynamics mix rapidly, and how do bounds on pairwise correlations propagate to the spectral gap of the chain?
setting: Distributions on labelings of the n vertices of a graph (spin systems such as the hard-core model on independent sets) and distributions over the bases of a matroid. Reversible discrete- and continuous-time Markov chains (Glauber dynamics / Gibbs sampler, bases-exchange walk). This is an expository monograph unifying a body of recent results.
method: Spectral independence: a bound on the maximum eigenvalue of the influence matrix that records the pairwise influence (closely related to covariance) between variables. Local-to-global theorems relate local walks on a simplicial complex, which encode pairwise correlations, to global variance decay and the spectral gap. Analysis is carried out from a functional-analysis / spectral-gap perspective; the Trickle-Down Theorem is reproven in the same Markov chain language.
contribution: A self-contained, unified presentation with full proofs showing spectral independence implies optimal mixing, applied to: Glauber dynamics on general graphs in the tree-uniqueness region, polynomial-time mixing at the uniqueness critical point, polynomial-time mixing on random regular graphs beyond the uniqueness threshold, and fast mixing of the bases-exchange walk for an arbitrary matroid.

mathematical_objects.name: Spectral independence
mathematical_objects.role: The central hypothesis: a bound on the top eigenvalue of the influence matrix, from which fast mixing is derived.

mathematical_objects.name: Influence matrix
mathematical_objects.role: Encodes how conditioning one variable shifts the marginal of another; spectral independence is a spectral bound on this object.

mathematical_objects.name: Glauber dynamics
mathematical_objects.role: The Markov chain whose spectral gap and mixing time the local-to-global machinery controls.

mathematical_objects.name: High-dimensional expander local walks
mathematical_objects.role: The intermediate objects: local walks at each level of the complex whose spectral gaps compose to the global mixing bound.

mathematical_objects.name: Modified log-Sobolev inequality
mathematical_objects.role: The functional-analytic quantity being bounded; its lower bound is equivalent to a mixing-time upper bound.

mathematical_objects.name: Trickle-Down Theorem
mathematical_objects.role: Propagates a local spectral bound at the top of the complex downward to all levels, supplying the base case for local-to-global.

mathematical_objects.name: Matroid basis-exchange walk
mathematical_objects.role: The second application domain, where spectral independence yields mixing for sampling a uniform random basis of any matroid.

limitations: Expository monograph, not a source of new theorems; it repackages and unifies existing results.
Extractor matched neither an introduction nor a conclusion heading; card is built from the abstract and the section list.
Focuses on spectral-gap (Poincare) analysis; entropy-decay / modified log-Sobolev arguments are covered less centrally.
Applications are limited to two model classes (spin systems and matroids).
open_questions: The abstract frames spectral independence and local-to-global as a general technique, but its reach to combinatorial distributions outside spin systems and matroids is not delimited here. This machinery is likely stronger than the two applications shown.
Which correlation-decay notions are exactly equivalent to spectral independence outside the tree-uniqueness setting.
cross_domain_note: Highest-value transfer category for this KB: any sampling-based estimator or MCMC method whose correctness rests on a mixing-time bound can potentially import spectral independence in place of ad hoc coupling arguments.

title: Stabilization by rough noise for an epitaxial growth model
problem: Does adding arbitrarily small space-time white noise to a phenomenological epitaxial thin-film growth SPDE (with a Schwoebel-barrier nonlinearity) change its qualitative long-time behavior, in particular the linear instability that drives the growth of hills on a flat surface?
setting: The SPDE d_t h = -delta * Bilaplacian(h) - div( grad h / (1 + |grad h|^2) ) + sigma * xi on the torus T^d, with xi space-time white noise (derivative of a cylindrical Wiener process), delta and sigma small positive parameters, zero spatial mean, dimensions d = 1, 2. The noise is only slightly too rough for direct fixed-point or Galerkin methods.
method: Regularization of the noise followed by a Da Prato-Debussche-type decomposition, with an explicit Fourier-series computation of the stochastic convolution. One shows that the nonlinear current, evaluated on the rough Gaussian solution, degenerates in the limit of vanishing regularization (renormalization, with the counterterms vanishing). The bilaplacian generates an analytic semigroup used for the mild formulation.
contribution: Shows that arbitrarily small space-time white noise eliminates all nonlinear interaction in this model: in the vanishing-regularization limit the equation collapses to its linear part, which is stable, so the noise suppresses hill growth. A stabilization-by-noise mechanism driven specifically by the spatial roughness of the noise, in the spirit of the Hairer-Ryser-Weber triviality results for the 2D Allen-Cahn equation.

mathematical_objects.name: Semilinear stochastic PDE
mathematical_objects.role: The object of study; a bilaplacian linear part plus a bounded non-polynomial gradient nonlinearity plus additive white noise.

mathematical_objects.name: Space-time white noise
mathematical_objects.role: The driving noise whose roughness is exactly the feature producing stabilization; its regularity sits just below what direct methods need.

mathematical_objects.name: Stochastic convolution
mathematical_objects.role: The Gaussian solution of the linearized equation, computed explicitly by Fourier series; the nonlinearity is evaluated against it.

mathematical_objects.name: Da Prato-Debussche decomposition
mathematical_objects.role: Splits the solution into the explicit rough Gaussian part and a smoother remainder, and organizes the limiting cancellation of the nonlinear term.

mathematical_objects.name: Analytic semigroup of the bilaplacian
mathematical_objects.role: Provides the smoothing needed for the mild formulation and existence and uniqueness of the regularized solution.

mathematical_objects.name: Gradient-flow energy functional
mathematical_objects.role: Characterizes the deterministic dynamics (attractor of equilibria and heteroclinics) against which the stochastic triviality is contrasted.

limitations: Conclusion section not matched by the extractor; card built from abstract and introduction.
Result is specific to this bounded non-polynomial Schwoebel current; it does not fit the standard polynomial-nonlinearity rough-SPDE framework.
Stated as 'potential to stabilize': the dynamical consequence is argued via triviality of the limit equation rather than a full long-time stochastic analysis.
Requires delta and sigma small; the physically interesting case d = 2 is the hardest.
open_questions: The triviality / stabilization mechanism here is proven for a bounded, non-polynomial nonlinear current. The paper notes that most rough-SPDE renormalization theory targets polynomial nonlinearities, so this technique is broader than the class of equations it is usually applied to. Which other non-polynomial nonlinearities collapse under sufficiently rough noise is open.
The stochastic motion of hills under the renormalized (linear) dynamics is not studied.
cross_domain_note: Stabilization-by-noise and SPDE triviality are portable phenomena; the same mechanism could bear on other surface-growth and pattern-formation models where a deterministic instability is assumed to persist under fluctuations.

title: Duality of causal distributionally robust optimization
problem: Can distributionally robust optimization be made tractable in a dynamic (multi-period / continuous-time) setting when the ambiguity set is a causal or adapted Wasserstein ball around a reference model rather than a standard Wasserstein ball?
setting: Stochastic processes in discrete and continuous time on a filtered space. Model uncertainty penalized by the causal or bicausal (adapted) Wasserstein distance, or a penalized variant. Objectives: worst-case linear expectation, worst-case expected shortfall (a concave nonlinear expectation), and worst-case value of an optimal stopping problem (in general not concave), the last in discrete time.
method: Convex / Lagrangian duality converting the penalized worst-case problem into inf over lambda >= 0 of L*(lambda) + U(lambda), where L* is the convex conjugate of the penalty and U is a convex function given by a dynamic programming principle. U is computed by a recursion in discrete time and by a path-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, derived via functional Ito calculus, in continuous time. Optimal stopping is handled by a concave relaxation lifting the problem to the space of adapted processes on a nested space, recasting it as a classical Wasserstein DRO.
contribution: First dynamic duality for causal DRO in continuous time; extension from worst-case expectation to worst-case expected shortfall (a nonlinear expectation); a relaxation recasting causal distributionally robust optimal stopping as Wasserstein DRO on a nested space; a proof that causal and bicausal penalizations are equivalent under mild conditions; a demonstration that the causal constraint shrinks the ambiguity set and reduces over-conservatism relative to standard Wasserstein DRO in dynamic problems.

mathematical_objects.name: Adapted Wasserstein distance
mathematical_objects.role: Defines the ambiguity set; it penalizes differences in the information flow of models, not only their spatial distance, which is what makes the dynamic problem well posed.

mathematical_objects.name: Causal optimal transport
mathematical_objects.role: The transport problem whose cost defines the ambiguity radius; its computational hardness is the obstacle the duality circumvents.

mathematical_objects.name: Distributionally robust optimization
mathematical_objects.role: The minimax framework being lifted to a dynamic setting.

mathematical_objects.name: Convex conjugate / Fenchel duality
mathematical_objects.role: Turns the penalized worst-case expectation into a one-dimensional minimization over the Lagrange multiplier lambda.

mathematical_objects.name: Path-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation
mathematical_objects.role: Characterizes the inner value function U in continuous time, obtained by treating the dual as a non-Markovian stochastic control problem.

mathematical_objects.name: Functional Ito calculus
mathematical_objects.role: Supplies the horizontal and vertical derivatives needed to write the path-dependent HJB equation.

mathematical_objects.name: Expected shortfall
mathematical_objects.role: The concave nonlinear objective functional to which the duality is extended beyond the linear expectation case.

mathematical_objects.name: Optimal stopping
mathematical_objects.role: The non-concave objective handled by the concave relaxation on the nested space of adapted processes.

limitations: Conclusion section not matched by the extractor; card built from abstract and introduction.
Continuous-time results need regularity conditions and the functional Ito framework.
The optimal stopping treatment is restricted to discrete time.
Value functions of optimal stopping are discontinuous in the standard Wasserstein topology, which motivates but also confines the causal approach.
open_questions: The adapted-Wasserstein ambiguity set is shown to be the correct object whenever the objective is discontinuous in the standard Wasserstein topology. This is a general signal: dynamic and sequential decision problems that currently use static Wasserstein DRO may be relying on an ambiguity set that is too large or ill-posed.
Which non-concave functionals beyond optimal stopping admit the concave nested-space relaxation.
cross_domain_note: Statistics and operations research use of Wasserstein DRO is largely static; this paper supplies the dynamic duality theory (recursion in discrete time, path-dependent HJB in continuous time).

title: The circular law for random band matrices with arbitrary doubly stochastic variance profile
problem: Does the empirical spectral distribution of a non-Hermitian random band matrix converge to the circular law when the bandwidth is a genuine power law n^gamma and the variance profile is only assumed doubly stochastic, with no mixing or structural conditions on the profile?
setting: n x n non-Hermitian matrices with independent entries; bandwidth scaling like n^gamma for gamma in (0,1]; variance profile doubly stochastic with no further assumption. Circular law proven for Gaussian entries when gamma > 5/6 and for subgaussian entries when gamma > 8/9. Asymptotics n -> infinity.
method: Girko Hermitization: control the log-determinant of X - z via the Stieltjes transform of the symmetrized resolvent of a linearized model, plus a convergence-rate estimate for that transform. The key new input is polynomial lower bounds on intermediate small singular values that do not use the profile structure beyond double stochasticity.
contribution: Lowers the bandwidth threshold for the circular law from gamma > 32/33 (which was known only for block and periodic band matrices) to gamma > 5/6 (Gaussian) and gamma > 8/9 (subgaussian), for an arbitrary doubly stochastic profile. Also proves an extended product circular law with a growing number of factors and weak eigenvector delocalization estimates.

mathematical_objects.name: Circular law
mathematical_objects.role: The limiting object whose validity under weak bandwidth and profile assumptions is the theorem being proven.

mathematical_objects.name: Empirical spectral distribution
mathematical_objects.role: The random measure whose weak convergence to the uniform measure on the disc is the statement of the result.

mathematical_objects.name: Hermitization (Girko's method)
mathematical_objects.role: Reduces the non-Hermitian eigenvalue problem to controlling the symmetrized resolvent and its log-determinant as a function of the spectral parameter z.

mathematical_objects.name: Smallest singular value lower bound
mathematical_objects.role: The technical crux: polynomial anti-concentration lower bounds on intermediate small singular values of X - z that hold uniformly over doubly stochastic profiles.

mathematical_objects.name: Stieltjes transform
mathematical_objects.role: Tracks the symmetrized spectral density; its quantitative convergence rate feeds the Hermitization estimate.

mathematical_objects.name: Doubly stochastic variance profile
mathematical_objects.role: The only structural assumption on the matrix of entry variances; the proof is engineered to depend on this and nothing more.

mathematical_objects.name: Random band matrix
mathematical_objects.role: The structured sparse non-Hermitian ensemble under study, prototype for Anderson-transition models in the non-Hermitian setting.

limitations: Conclusion section was not matched by the extractor; framing rests on abstract and introduction.
Threshold gamma > 5/6 is still far from the conjectured regime (gamma > 1/2 or even any positive power).
Subgaussian case is weaker (gamma > 8/9) than the Gaussian case.
Requires the profile to be exactly doubly stochastic; later work by the author handles smaller gamma only under specific mixing properties.
open_questions: The polynomial small-singular-value lower bound is explicitly stated to be independent of the variance profile beyond double stochasticity. This is reusable machinery: it is stronger than its use here and should transfer to other sparse inhomogeneous non-Hermitian ensembles where the smallest singular value is the bottleneck.
Whether the power-law bandwidth threshold can be pushed toward gamma > 1/2 for arbitrary doubly stochastic profiles.
cross_domain_note: Non-Hermitian band matrices are the global-universality analogue of the Hermitian Anderson-transition models used in mathematical physics; the singular value estimate is the portable piece.

title: Queueing models with random resetting
problem: How can the stationary distributions and standard performance measures of queueing systems that clear (reset to the empty state) at random times be characterized explicitly, for both Markovian and non-Markovian service and arrival processes?
setting: FCFS discipline throughout. Markovian models: M/M/r and M/M/1+M queues with a resetting transition to state 0 added to the birth-death dynamics, giving a continuous-time Markov chain that is no longer a birth-death process. Non-Markovian models: GI/GI/1, GI/GI/r and GI/GI/infinity queues with resetting to zero at arrival epochs.
method: For the CTMC models, partial balance equations are solved to give the stationary law as an integral representation plus a terminating generalized hypergeometric sum, the two pieces obeying the same recursion with different boundary conditions. For GI/GI/1 and GI/GI/r, modified Lindley and Kiefer-Wolfowitz recursions are introduced and written in operator form, from which the stationary distribution is expressed as a convergent series solving a modified Wiener-Hopf equation. For GI/GI/infinity, an adapted Kiefer-Wolfowitz recursion on the vector of elapsed service times is used.
contribution: Explicit stationary distributions for the M/M/r queue with resetting for general r (new) and for the M/M/1+M queue with resetting (new); a proof that resetting makes the queueing CTMC positive recurrent for any traffic intensity, even zero service rate; a unified operator/series characterization for GI/GI/1 and GI/GI/r with resetting that holds whether or not the underlying queue is stable; and an explicit stationary law for GI/GI/infinity with resetting.

mathematical_objects.name: Continuous-time Markov chain
aliases: birth-death process with an added jump to zero
mathematical_objects.role: The state process for the Markovian models; adding the resetting transition breaks the birth-death structure but keeps an explicitly solvable stationary law.

mathematical_objects.name: Partial balance equations
mathematical_objects.role: The tool used to guess and verify the stationary distribution of the resetting CTMC without a birth-death product form.

mathematical_objects.name: Lindley recursion
mathematical_objects.role: The waiting-time recursion for GI/GI/1; its modified version incorporates resetting at arrival epochs.

mathematical_objects.name: Kiefer-Wolfowitz recursion
mathematical_objects.role: The multi-server workload-vector recursion for GI/GI/r and, adapted, for GI/GI/infinity; modified to include resetting.

mathematical_objects.name: Wiener-Hopf equation
mathematical_objects.role: Characterizes the stationary waiting-time law; the resetting models satisfy a modified Wiener-Hopf equation solved by a convergent operator series.

mathematical_objects.name: Stochastic resetting
mathematical_objects.role: The mechanism under study: instantaneous return of the system to the empty state at random (here Poisson or arrival-triggered) times.

mathematical_objects.name: Positive recurrence / stationary distribution
mathematical_objects.role: The property established unconditionally under resetting, in contrast to the traffic-intensity-below-one requirement for standard queues.

limitations: Resetting is restricted to the empty state, and in the non-Markovian case to arrival epochs.
Heavy-traffic diffusion approximations of reset queues are not treated.
Some stationary laws are given as convergent series that may not be numerically transparent.
No transient analysis for general r.
open_questions: Resetting induces positive recurrence regardless of traffic intensity. The paper leaves open a general Markov-chain-level characterization of which resetting mechanisms guarantee ergodicity, and whether explicit stationary laws survive for broader classes (forthcoming work is announced).
Diffusion / heavy-traffic limits of reset queues and the ergodic properties and stationary laws of the limiting reflected diffusions.
cross_domain_note: Stochastic resetting is heavily studied in statistical physics (search processes, resetting random walks); this paper supplies the queueing-theory side with exact stationary analysis and the observation that resetting is a universal stabilizer.

title: Multi-Dimensional Opinion Formation
problem: How do opinions evolve when agents hold positions on several related topics simultaneously and also assign individual importance weights to those topics, with the update on any one topic depending on similarity across the whole opinion vector?
setting: A large population of agents, each carrying an opinion vector and an importance-weight vector over the topics. Opinions change through binary interactions; the change on one topic is governed by a weighted similarity computed from the full opinion vector. Studied at the kinetic level and in the mean-field (large-population) limit.
method: A kinetic (Boltzmann-type) equation for the interaction rule, from which a nonlocal mean-field partial differential equation for the population density is derived in a grazing / mean-field limit. Stationary states and qualitative dynamics are studied by analytical computation and numerical simulation.
contribution: Introduces the weighted cross-topic similarity and the associated coupling mechanism; derives the mean-field PDE; shows that individual importance weights critically determine the stationary opinion structure (a variety of states beyond consensus), and that with heterogeneous weights the average opinion vector can drift and the variance can grow, behavior absent under a plain Euclidean distance.

mathematical_objects.name: Kinetic equation
mathematical_objects.role: Encodes the binary-interaction rule at the population level and is the starting point for the limit.

mathematical_objects.name: Mean-field limit
mathematical_objects.role: Passes from the kinetic description to a closed PDE for the one-agent density; the derivation is the probabilistic content of the paper.

mathematical_objects.name: Interacting particle system
mathematical_objects.role: The microscopic stochastic dynamics: randomly paired agents update opinions according to the weighted-similarity rule.

mathematical_objects.name: Nonlocal transport PDE
mathematical_objects.role: The mean-field object whose stationary solutions classify the possible long-time opinion configurations.

mathematical_objects.name: Stationary states
mathematical_objects.role: The equilibria of the mean-field PDE; their dependence on the weight distribution is the main qualitative finding.

mathematical_objects.name: Weighted similarity metric
mathematical_objects.role: Replaces the Euclidean opinion distance; its asymmetry across agents is what lets the mean opinion drift and the variance increase.

limitations: Primary listing is physics.soc-ph; the probabilistic content is essentially the mean-field derivation, and the analysis is PDE-flavored.
Convergence to steady state with heterogeneous importance weights is not proved.
Full characterization of the stationary states is left open.
No quantitative mean-field error bound or propagation-of-chaos statement.
open_questions: Rigorous propagation of chaos and a quantitative mean-field error for this weighted-coupling interaction are not established; the kinetic-to-PDE step is formal.
Convergence rate to steady state under heterogeneous importance weights, and full classification of stationary states.
cross_domain_note: Charter blind spot: this sits at the boundary between probability (mean-field limits of interacting particle systems) and applied PDE / socio-physics. Carded here because the transferable object is the mean-field derivation for a non-metric, weighted interaction kernel.

title: Quantum Markovian Dynamics from a Double Covariance Stochastic Framework
problem: Can the standard evolution equations of quantum theory (the Lindblad master equation for open systems, the von Neumann equation for closed systems) be derived from classical correlated stochastic processes on subsystem Hilbert spaces via coarse-graining, rather than postulated?
setting: Local Ito stochastic differential equations on subsystem Hilbert spaces. Two separated time scales: a fast microscopic fluctuation scale with correlation time of order epsilon^2 and a slower macroscopic averaging window of order epsilon. The macroscopic dynamics is obtained in the hydrodynamic limit epsilon -> 0. Interacting composite systems are modeled by local, state-dependent stochastic feedback fields.
method: Multi-scale Ito calculus combined with sliding-window time averaging to derive a closed evolution equation for a coarse-grained double covariance operator (a fourth-order statistical object: covariance of microscopic time-window correlations). A homogenization / hydrodynamic limit removes the fast fluctuations; the deterministic drift yields the Hamiltonian commutator and the quadratic-variation (noise covariance) terms yield the dissipative channels.
contribution: Shows the normalized double covariance obeys exactly the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad equation, with unitary von Neumann evolution recovered as the fluctuation-free limit; demonstrates that non-separable interaction Hamiltonians can emerge from strictly local state-dependent stochastic feedback; provides a single classical-stochastic foundation for both open and closed quantum dynamics, in contrast to noncommutative quantum stochastic calculus.

mathematical_objects.name: Ito stochastic differential equation
mathematical_objects.role: The microscopic law for the subquantum processes on each subsystem Hilbert space; the starting point of the construction.

mathematical_objects.name: Quadratic variation
mathematical_objects.role: The bracket terms that, after coarse-graining, become the dissipative (Lindblad) part of the macroscopic generator.

mathematical_objects.name: Multi-scale homogenization limit
mathematical_objects.role: Sends the ratio of microscopic correlation time to averaging window to zero, killing fast fluctuations and leaving a deterministic transport equation.

mathematical_objects.name: GKSL generator
mathematical_objects.role: The target macroscopic equation shown to emerge exactly from the two-scale stochastic dynamics.

mathematical_objects.name: Covariance operator
mathematical_objects.role: The coarse-grained state object that plays the role of the density operator and whose evolution equation is derived.

mathematical_objects.name: Sliding-window time averaging
mathematical_objects.role: The coarse-graining operation that separates macroscopic observables from microscopic fluctuations.

limitations: Conclusion is very brief; the paper is a physics reconstruction program and the rigor of the epsilon -> 0 limit is relegated to an appendix, not assessable from the extract.
Relies on the specific scaling (window of order epsilon, correlation time of order epsilon^2).
The subquantum interpretation is model-specific; portability rests on the averaging argument, not the physical framing.
Confidence low: statistical-physics-adjacent, limited visible rigor.
open_questions: The claim that dissipative structure arises purely from quadratic noise correlations under a two-scale limit is a homogenization statement that could be isolated and proved as a standalone stochastic-averaging theorem, independent of any quantum interpretation. Its hypotheses are stronger than needed for that abstract statement.
Conditions under which the coarse-grained equation is genuinely Markovian (closed) rather than memory-dependent.
cross_domain_note: The transferable content is a two-scale stochastic averaging / homogenization result in which fast quadratic noise correlations produce a deterministic dissipative limit; the quantum master equation is one instantiation.

title: Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos for i.i.d. matrices
problem: Do fractional powers of the absolute characteristic polynomial of a non-Hermitian random matrix with i.i.d. entries converge to Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos, for a non-invariant ensemble with no exact eigenvalue formula, across the full subcritical regime?
setting: N x N matrices X with i.i.d. entries (real or complex), variance 1/N. The random measure mu_N(z) = |det(X - z)|^gamma / E|det(X - z)|^gamma dz dz-bar on the unit disc, gamma in the full subcritical range (0, 2 sqrt 2), N -> infinity. Both symmetry classes.
method: Analytic and probabilistic techniques with a dynamical component: Dyson Brownian motion for the Hermitized matrix, the matrix Dyson equation and Hermitization, and local laws. The K-point function of |det(X - z)| is analyzed at any collection of mesoscopically separated points, and its asymptotics drive the convergence to GMC.
contribution: First proof of convergence to Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos for a non-invariant, non-integrable random matrix ensemble; covers the entire subcritical range and both symmetry classes (new even for the real Ginibre ensemble); for real matrices also proves that the restriction of the measure to the unit interval converges to a one-dimensional GMC; establishes K-point function asymptotics at mesoscopic separation.

mathematical_objects.name: Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos
mathematical_objects.role: The limiting random fractal measure; the theorem is its identification as the limit of normalized powers of the characteristic polynomial.

mathematical_objects.name: Log-correlated Gaussian field
mathematical_objects.role: The limit of the log-characteristic polynomial (Rider-Virag); its log-correlated covariance is what makes the GMC construction applicable.

mathematical_objects.name: Characteristic polynomial
mathematical_objects.role: The random-matrix observable whose fractional power is exponentiated to form mu_N; its fluctuations are the log-correlated field.

mathematical_objects.name: Dyson Brownian motion
mathematical_objects.role: The dynamical device: interpolating the ensemble along a matrix Ornstein-Uhlenbeck flow to prove the required correlation-function asymptotics without invariance.

mathematical_objects.name: Matrix Dyson equation
mathematical_objects.role: Reduces the non-Hermitian problem to a self-consistent equation for the symmetrized resolvent, supplying the local law inputs.

mathematical_objects.name: K-point correlation function
mathematical_objects.role: The joint asymptotics of |det(X - z_i)| at mesoscopically separated points, the quantitative core from which GMC convergence is deduced.

mathematical_objects.name: Circular law
mathematical_objects.role: The zeroth-order eigenvalue limit around which the log-characteristic polynomial fluctuates; sets the normalization of mu_N.

limitations: Conclusion section not matched by the extractor; card built from abstract and introduction.
Subcritical regime gamma < 2 sqrt 2 only; the critical and supercritical cases remain open.
Requires i.i.d. entries; the moment / regularity assumptions in the body are not visible in the extract.
K-point asymptotics are at mesoscopic, not microscopic, separation.
open_questions: The method is explicitly built to avoid integrability and invariance, and the authors frame it as extendable to broad classes of generic ensembles. How far it reaches (band matrices, heavy-tailed entries, sparse ensembles) is open, and the result is stronger than the invariant-ensemble literature it supersedes.
Critical and supercritical gamma; and whether the still-open subcritical GMC convergence for GOE and GSE follows from these techniques.
cross_domain_note: Log-correlated fields and their GMC / extreme-value structure connect to analytic number theory (models for the Riemann zeta function), Liouville quantum gravity and 2D conformal field theory.

title: Identifiability and Estimation for Unlabeled Finite Mixtures under Marginal Independence
problem: When can the latent component distributions, and the mixing matrix, of several unlabeled finite mixtures that share components but have unknown mixing weights be recovered, using only the assumption that each component is independent on at least one coordinate pair?
setting: Several observable mixture distributions over the same latent components with unknown weights. No labels, no clean component samples, no known proportions, no parametric component families. Each component assumed marginally independent for at least one pair of coordinates. Both a population identifiability question and a finite-sample estimation question are treated; experiments on synthetic data and flow cytometry.
method: Structural identifiability via a subset-rank condition on the spans of the univariate marginals: any fully independent distribution in the affine span of product-form components must coincide with a single component, so the intersection of the affine mixture space with the independence model is discrete. This is extended to coordinate-pair (marginal) independence under no-cancellation and full-rank conditions. Estimation uses a Product-Marginal Maximum Mean Discrepancy criterion (comparing a candidate's bivariate marginal with the product of its one-dimensional marginals via a characteristic kernel), minimized over signed affine combinations of the observable mixtures. Kernel mean embedding deviation bounds give uniform convergence and stability under approximate marginal independence.
contribution: Identifiability theorem for mixtures of marginally independent components from unlabeled multi-mixtures, recovering components and (under completion conditions) the mixing matrix; the PM-MMD estimator with proven uniform convergence and stability; a clean separation of the empirical status of the assumptions (marginal independence yields a held-out candidate-level diagnostic, whereas irreducibility is not testable from unlabeled mixtures alone).

mathematical_objects.name: Finite mixture model
mathematical_objects.role: The object being identified: shared latent components combined with unknown per-mixture weight vectors collected in the mixing matrix.

mathematical_objects.name: Marginal independence
mathematical_objects.role: The identifying signal: independence on one coordinate pair per component, strictly weaker than the full independence usually assumed.

mathematical_objects.name: Kernel mean embedding
mathematical_objects.role: Represents each candidate distribution as a Hilbert-space element so that the independence gap is a norm; deviation bounds for empirical embeddings drive the statistical guarantees.

mathematical_objects.name: Maximum Mean Discrepancy
mathematical_objects.role: The discrepancy between a candidate's bivariate marginal and the product of its one-dimensional marginals; its population zero set characterizes the recoverable components.

mathematical_objects.name: Characteristic kernel
mathematical_objects.role: Ensures the MMD is zero exactly when the marginal is a product, making the criterion a valid independence measure.

mathematical_objects.name: Subset-rank and no-cancellation conditions
mathematical_objects.role: Affine-span geometric conditions guaranteeing the independence constraint isolates a single component rather than a spurious combination.

mathematical_objects.name: Uniform concentration of empirical embeddings
mathematical_objects.role: Converts pointwise embedding deviation bounds into uniform control over the whole affine search domain, giving the estimator its convergence rate.

limitations: Each component must be independent on some coordinate pair; components with no such pair are not identifiable by this route.
The no-cancellation condition is essential and is shown empirically to fail badly when violated.
The empirical MMD objective is nonconvex; solvers are heuristic.
Finite-sample analysis of the validation and condition-aware selection steps is left to future work.
Irreducibility is used to complete the mixing matrix but is acknowledged to be untestable from unlabeled mixtures.
open_questions: The identifiability argument uses only marginal (pairwise) independence, not the full independence assumed in most mixture and ICA identifiability results. This is a genuinely weaker structural assumption than the literature imposes and the transferable content of the paper.
Finite-sample rates for the representative-selection step, and automatic selection of the informative coordinate pairs.
cross_domain_note: Sits between probability (concentration for kernel mean embeddings, uniform laws over function classes), statistics (mixture identifiability and estimation) and machine learning (weak supervision, label-shift). The portable probabilistic pieces are the embedding deviation bounds and the uniform convergence argument; the asymptotic behavior of the estimator itself is a statistics question.
